paper_metadata.title: Real Option Pricing using Quantum Computers

summary: The paper studies gate-based quantum option pricing via quantum accelerated Monte Carlo on a Black-Scholes model, using a 32-point discretization that requires 5 qubits for the distribution register plus 1 ancilla in the extracted setup. It reports emulator-based results for European call, put, and digital options, and shows that direct encoding with mRQAE can handle sign-changing payoffs better than naive square-root encoding, but no practical quantum advantage over classical Monte Carlo is demonstrated.
